title: Hashmatullah Shahidi Resigns as Afghanistan's ODI Captain Ahead of Ireland Series
excerpt: The veteran left-hander steps down from the ODI leadership role just before a crucial series against Ireland, adding to Afghanistan cricket's long history of captaincy upheaval driven by selection disputes with the ACB.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Hashmatullah Shahidi resigns as Afghanistan's ODI captain ahead of the Ireland series.
  • Afghanistan cricket faces ongoing captaincy turmoil due to ACB's selection interference.
  • Shahidi remains Afghanistan's Test captain and will continue playing ODIs.
  • Hashmatullah Shahidi has resigned as Afghanistan's ODI captain just ahead of the upcoming Ireland series, according to ESPNCricinfo.
  • The decision continues Afghanistan cricket's troubled pattern of captaincy changes, with selection interference by the Afghanistan Cricket Board (ACB) a recurring flashpoint.
  • Shahidi remains Afghanistan's Test captain and is expected to continue playing as a batter in ODIs.

Shahidi Steps Down After Five Years at the Helm

Hashmatullah Shahidi has resigned as Afghanistan's ODI captain ahead of the team's upcoming series against Ireland, ESPNCricinfo reported on Monday. The 31-year-old left-handed batter, who was appointed ODI and Test captain in May 2021 after the Afghanistan Cricket Board removed Asghar Afghan, had led the side in the 50-over format for over five years.

https://x.com/cricinfo/status/2079633007410135171

Shahidi's resignation comes at a turbulent time for Afghanistan cricket, which has undergone a sweeping overhaul following its early exit from the T20 World Cup 2026. The ACB sacked head coach Jonathan Trott and replaced him with Richard Pybus, removed Rashid Khan as T20I captain in favour of Ibrahim Zadran, and saw veteran all-rounder Mohammad Nabi announce his retirement from international cricket after 17 years.

"As the captain and responsible person for the nation, I deserve the right to be part of the selection of the team."

— Rashid Khan, on stepping down as T20I captain in 2021 over selection disputes with the ACB
> **"Asghar Afghan was sacked and reinstated multiple times, and a split-captaincy model was implemented and abandoned repeatedly."**

"Asghar Afghan was sacked and reinstated multiple times, and a split-captaincy model was implemented and abandoned repeatedly."

A Pattern of Captaincy Upheaval

Shahidi's departure from the captaincy fits a well-documented pattern within Afghanistan cricket, where selection interference by the ACB has repeatedly driven captains to resign or be sacked. Rashid Khan famously stepped down as T20I captain in 2021 hours after the T20 World Cup squad was announced without his consultation. Mohammad Nabi, who replaced Rashid as T20I captain, also cited disagreements with the selection committee when he resigned during the 2022 T20 World Cup.

Before Shahidi's appointment, the ACB had already cycled through multiple captaincy structures. Asghar Afghan was sacked and reinstated multiple times, and a split-captaincy model was implemented and abandoned repeatedly. Cricbuzz has described selection interference as "Afghanistan's Achilles heel," noting that the ACB's revolving-door approach to captaincy has prevented leaders from establishing authority.

"The selection panel wanted them and this was one of the main reasons behind his decision to quit," an ACB official told Cricbuzz about Nabi's resignation, in comments that could apply equally to the broader culture of captaincy disputes within the board.

Shahidi's Record as Captain

Shahidi has been a steady presence in Afghanistan's batting lineup since his ODI debut against Kenya in October 2013. In 96 ODIs, the Logar-born batter has scored 2,607 runs at an average of 33.42, including one century and 22 half-centuries. His highest ODI score of 102 came during the third ODI against India in Chennai in June 2026, where he anchored Afghanistan's chase before running into trouble with the ICC for repeatedly running on the protected area of the pitch.

In Test cricket, where he is expected to continue as captain, Shahidi has been even more impressive. Across 12 Tests, he has scored 796 runs at an average of 44.22, including a historic double century of 246 — making him the first Afghan player to score a Test double hundred, achieved against Zimbabwe in March 2021.

What It Means for the Afghan Diaspora

For the large Afghan diaspora in India and beyond, captaincy changes are more than just cricket news. They reflect the institutional instability that continues to shadow the ACB under Taliban governance. Afghan cricket fans across South Asia and the diaspora have watched with frustration as the board's internal politics have undermined the on-field progress of a team that reached the T20 World Cup semi-finals in 2024 and continues to produce world-class talent like Rashid Khan, Rahmanullah Gurbaz, and Ibrahim Zadran.

What's Next

The ACB has not yet announced a successor for the ODI captaincy. Rahmat Shah, who has served as vice-captain in ODIs and Tests, and Ibrahim Zadran, the current T20I captain, are among the potential candidates. Afghanistan's upcoming Ireland series will be the first test of the team's new leadership structure in the 50-over format, as the side looks to rebuild stability ahead of a packed international calendar.
